These medications are glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, meaning that they “mimic” natural GLP-1 to activate these GLP-1 receptors in the brain and the gastrointestinal system to promote satiety and reduced gastric emptying. However, there has been evidence that Ozempic (and other GLP-1 receptor agonists) may cause psychological side effects, which we discuss in this lesson. I hope you find this lesson helpful. If you do, please like and subscribe for more lessons like this one! JJ NOTE: Most of these studies are only case studies, so not strong evidence - more research is needed to see if there is a relationship between psychological side effects and Ozempic use.
